minor.issue: Locale default mismatch: /app/backend/.env sets APP_LOCALE=en and APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE=en, while the content default locale is 'id' (setting general.default_locale = 'id'). PublicContentController::resolveLocale() falls back to config('app.fallback_locale') so a request without ?locale returns ENGLISH content (verified: GET /public/faqs returns 'How long does it take to build a website?' vs locale=id 'Berapa lama proses pembuatan website?'). Admin lists also render the EN translation, so a record whose EN row omits optional fields shows '—' in the table even though the Indonesian values exist. Recommend resolving the default from Locale::defaultCode()/general.default_locale (or set APP_LOCALE/APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE=id) and adding per-field fallback in HasTranslations::translated().
Fallback is row-level only: when the requested locale row exists but a field is null, no fallback to the default locale field happens (name/role/company render as '—').

action_items: Decide and fix the default locale: make public API + admin resource serialization default to 'id' (Locale::defaultCode() / general.default_locale) instead of config('app.fallback_locale')='en'
Add per-field translation fallback in HasTranslations::translated() so partially filled locales do not render empty cells
critical_code_review_comments: PublicContentController::resolveLocale() should not depend on config('app.fallback_locale'); the CMS already stores general.default_locale = 'id'.
Admin list endpoints have no pagination (Testimonial/Service/Faq index use ->get()); acceptable for current data volumes but will not scale — consider per_page like the projects module.
SettingController::update() silently skips a row when the first() lookup returns null; the UpdateSettingsRequest guard covers it today, but a 404/422 on miss would be safer.

rca_of_the_issue: Locale issue root cause: backend/.env has APP_LOCALE=en / APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE=en, so app()->getLocale() is 'en' everywhere and PublicContentController::resolveLocale() returns 'en' when no ?locale is supplied; HasTranslations::translate() therefore picks the EN row whenever it exists, and falls back only per-row (not per-field) to Locale::defaultCode(). Reproduce: curl $BASE/api/v1/public/faqs (English) vs curl $BASE/api/v1/public/faqs?locale=id (Indonesian).
